summary: Douglas County, OR 40-foot L-4 tower, built 1934 or 1937 (sources differ), removed or destroyed 1963; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 40-foot pole L-4 tower (Oregon lookouts page: L-4 lookout house on a 40-foot round timber tower)
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1963 according to the sources; a directory of standing Oregon lookouts does not list it. No source describes what remains.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

events.note: Built 1934 per the register and Firelookout.com
Oregon lookouts page dates the L-4 lookout house to 1937; conflicts with 1934
John Hutchinson described as Forest Service lookout at Coffin Butte (Roseburg News-Review item, September 12, 1938)
Lookout station used for several days during a forest fire in the vicinity (News-Review item, November 1938); fire not named
Lookout injured chopping wood and carried out from the remote post by packhorse (Oregon Statesman item, July 1939)
Elinor Sherk driven to Tiller to assume duties as fire lookout at Coffin Butte (News-Review item, July 1952)
Deteriorated; disposal called for; two men given the job of destroying it (Oregon lookouts page); Firelookout.com says destroyed 1963
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register December 9, 2010

corrections.why: Firelookout.com gives the elevation as 4208 feet, which is about 1282.6 m. The brief's 1310.6 m equals about 4300 feet. No other source read gives an elevation, so check against a survey or topo map before changing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Firelookout.com give 1934; the Oregon lookouts page gives 1937 for the L-4 lookout house. The story reports both and does not choose.
The register says removed in 1963; Firelookout.com and the Oregon lookouts page say destroyed or disposed of in 1963. The year agrees; the verb differs.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict (1934 vs 1937) unresolved. Newspaper items are quoted second-hand from the Oregon lookouts page; the original News-Review and Oregon Statesman issues were not checked. The story names only John Hutchinson and Elinor Sherk; the 1939 injured lookout is left unnamed on purpose. No source describes the site today or public access. Do not confuse with the Coffin Butte landfill in northern Benton County (a search snippet from hh-today.com), which is a different place. The elevation correction is flagged for a human check. Staffing as_of 1952 is the last staffing mention found, not a current status.
